newThird.concept: A philosophical and mental-health route studies mind, emotion, agency and moral responsibility alongside historical and biopsychosocial approaches to mental disorder, clinical assessment and treatment. Cognitive science, empirical methods and social theory make competing accounts of mental life available for critical inquiry. Clinical courses provide complementary psychological study rather than a dedicated philosophy-of-psychiatry or neurodiversity sequence, and do not confer a clinical qualification.
newThird.judgment: Third mental-health concept considered before its course implementation; evaluate genuine response and scope rather than merely course-count difference.

conceptReassessment.reason: The current psychopathology profile explicitly includes historical views, classification and biopsychosocial explanations. Together with actual philosophy of mind, emotions, agency, ethics and clinical/cognitive content, it supports a distinct philosophical/mental-health response. It does not assert a complete psychiatric-philosophy or neurodiversity module, nor clinical qualification. A missing specialist title is not treated as sufficient rejection evidence.
conceptReassessment.implementationChanges: The proposed schedule exposed two offering conflicts. Psycholinguistics moved to its documentedSpring2027term; AIethics moved toSpring2029. The broader neurobiology option was reconsidered: brain/behaviour and cognitive study already supply biological foundations, while Logic/DiscreteMathematics adds substantive formal reasoning. This keeps the concept coherent under actual offerings without restoring superseded planning data.
conceptReassessment.remainingCandidates: Split the previously grouped animal/sociality, intercultural/decolonial and gender/feminist interests into three separately named candidates with their own generators/support. All remain evidenced; maximum-reached records the ceiling after three supported alternatives, not a fabricated failure of those directions.
